Meta Test Description: The testcase performs PCIe device enumeration across two dual-mode controllers (DM0 and DM1). It begins by writing 0x0 to 0xE6004100 to initialize the system. It then invokes link training (link_training_dm0_x4 or link_training_dm1_x4) based on compile-time defines (DM0_RC, DM1_RC, DM0_EP, DM1_EP). Cache coherency programming is performed by reading mizar_PCIE0_DBI_DSP_COHERENCY_CONTROL_3_OFF and mizar_PCIE1_DBI_DSP_COHERENCY_CONTROL_3_OFF, modifying specific bit fields using set_data at bit positions [11:14], [3:6], [27:30], and [19:22] with value 0xf, and writing back. A wait_on(20) delay is inserted between coherency programming phases. The test then polls read_sii0_reg(0xC0) in a while loop until (data_rd & 0xD1) == 0xD1, and similarly polls read_sii1_reg(0xC0) for the same link-up condition. Under DM0_RC, the Vendor ID is read from read_pcie_slv0_reg(0x0), the command register is written via write_pcie_slv0_reg(0x4, 0x7) to enable IO, Memory, and Bus Master, and memory base programming functions mem_base_program_dm0_x4 and mem_base_program_dm1_x4 are called. System-level registers at 0xE690000C, 0xE6900010, 0xE6900014, 0xE6900018, 0xE6900030, and 0xE6900034 are written with 0x1. Cache coherency is then disabled by writing 0x0 to bit fields [19:22] and [27:30] of both COHERENCY_CONTROL_3_OFF registers. After a wait_on(30), BAR sizing is performed on the endpoint via write_pcie_slv1_reg and read_pcie_slv1_reg for offsets 0x10, 0x14, 0x18, 0x1c, 0x20, 0x24 by writing 0xFFFFFFFF, reading back, then writing actual base addresses. The same BAR sizing sequence is repeated for slv0. Finally, the test polls 0xE6004100 in a while loop until the value equals 0x12345678, then calls finish(0).

Test Description: Verifies PCIe DMA write and read data transfer operations across four channels on the configured dual-mode controller. The interrupt handler reads DMA_WRITE_INT_STATUS_OFF and DMA_READ_INT_STATUS_OFF to determine which channels completed, then clears the interrupts via DMA_WRITE_INT_CLEAR_OFF and DMA_READ_INT_CLEAR_OFF. The test validates that all eight DMA transfers complete successfully via interrupt signaling.

Meta Test Description: The testcase performs register reset-value verification and write-read validation across multiple PCIe register groups on both PCIE0 and PCIE1 controllers.
Test Description: Verifies register reset default values and write-read data integrity for PCIe DBI controller registers, SII interface registers, and PHY registers across both PCIe controllers. The test first reads all target registers and compares against expected default values. It then writes multiple test patterns to MSI_CAP_OFF_08H_REG, MSI_CAP_OFF_10H_REG, FILTER_MASK_2_OFF, AXI_MSTR_MSG_ADDR_HIGH_OFF, UTILITY_OFF, SII interface registers, and PHY registers, reads them back, and verifies the written data matches the expected values after applying appropriate write masks. The test reports pass if all register values match expectations, or fail if any mismatch is detected.
Meta Test Steps / Procedure: 1-11. Define register address arrays, default values, and write masks. 12-20. chk_rst_val: read all registers and compare against defaults, bring PHY out of reset. 21-38. chk_rd_wr: write 3 test patterns to all register groups, read back and compare with expected masked values. Call finish(err2 || err1).
Test Steps / Procedure: 1. Read all target DBI controller registers for both PCIe controllers and verify they contain the expected reset default values. 2. Read all target SII interface registers for both controllers and verify reset default values. 3. Bring the PHY out of reset by writing to the PHY reset control registers for both controllers. 4. Read all target PHY registers for both controllers, extract the relevant bit fields using alignment-based masking, and verify reset default values. 5. For each of three test data patterns, write the pattern to all DBI controller registers (MSI_CAP_OFF_08H_REG, MSI_CAP_OFF_10H_REG, FILTER_MASK_2_OFF, AXI_MSTR_MSG_ADDR_HIGH_OFF, UTILITY_OFF) on both controllers. 6. Write the masked test pattern to all SII interface registers on both controllers using the appropriate write masks. 7. Write the PHY-specific test pattern to all PHY registers on both controllers using the PHY write masks. 8. Read back all DBI controller registers and verify the read data matches the written pattern. 9. Read back all SII interface registers and verify the read data matches the masked written pattern. 10. Read back all PHY registers, extract the relevant bit fields, and verify the read data matches the masked PHY pattern. 11. Repeat steps 5-10 for all remaining test patterns. 12. Report pass if no mismatches were detected across all reset-value checks and write-read checks; otherwise report fail.

Validation / Acceptance Criteria: The test passes when: (1) All DBI controller registers on both PCIe controllers read back their expected reset default values during the reset-value check phase. (2) All SII interface registers on both controllers read back their expected reset default values. (3) All PHY registers on both controllers read back their expected reset default values after PHY reset is released. (4) For each of the three write-read test patterns, all DBI controller registers (MSI_CAP_OFF_08H_REG, MSI_CAP_OFF_10H_REG, FILTER_MASK_2_OFF, AXI_MSTR_MSG_ADDR_HIGH_OFF, UTILITY_OFF) read back the exact written value on both controllers. Remarks: The testcase validates three distinct register groups: DBI controller registers, SII interface registers, and PHY registers across both PCIe controllers. PHY registers use alignment-based bit extraction where non-4-byte-aligned addresses require a 16-bit right shift and 4-byte-aligned addresses use a lower 16-bit mask. SII registers use per-register write masks to account for reserved or read-only bit fields. The PHY reset control register must be written before PHY registers can be accessed. Three test data patterns are used for DBI and SII registers, while three separate PHY-specific patterns are used for PHY registers. Several SII macros, PHY reset control macros, and PHY register addresses could not be mapped to the provided specification.
